correctness.rationale: Concavity justifies unrestricted symmetry reduction, not an assumption of uniformity. The 2-by-2 block spectrum has a monotone lower branch, and a sharp AM-GM bound yields the exact optimum, with unique invariant equality. A PSD-kernel equality argument across rotations forces every sunlet optimizer to have both first sine/cosine modes as eigenvectors; the leaf equations fix all pendant rates and the complex cycle equation fixes all rim rates. Selected exact symbolic checks and 1263 reproducible numerical/symbolic tests passed; the universal statement rests on the proof.

evidence: Sun et al. (2006) provides the general convex SDP, not a stronger closed-form corona theorem among its specific examples.
Boyd et al. (2007), theorem 3.1 and sections 2-3, handles a discrete-time SLEM problem on edge-transitive graphs; the enlarged corona is not edge-transitive and the optimization is different.
Barik et al. (2007), theorem 3.2 and corollary 3.5, describe unweighted corona Laplacian spectra and Fiedler vectors, with no optimization of independent edge conductances.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic optimization methods and spectral decomposition are inputs to the proof rather than results covering the precise formula. No inspected stronger continuous-time theorem has the same assumptions and conclusion; the sunlet rigidity proof uses equality across two Fourier modes in addition to routine symmetrization.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new implication is the explicit value B/(2e/mu+nc+2sqrt(enc/mu)) with strictly positive optimum rates for arbitrary individually adjustable edges and uniqueness for all sunlet rates. The exact eigenvalue formula alone is insufficient; it must be combined with a sharp resource dual inequality and, for uniqueness, a PSD-kernel equality argument.

evidence: Sun et al. (2006), section 1, defines the general cost-constrained Laplacian eigenvalue maximization, but sections 5.1-5.3 discuss a small graph, paths and the bare cycle; no leaf corona allocation formula appears in these inspected examples.

Boyd et al. (2007), arXiv:0709.0955, section 1 defines SLEM for discrete-time P and sections 2-3 reduce the discrete-time stochastic optimization by symmetry. This is a different feasible set and spectral objective.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same graph may admit a discrete-time SLEM optimization, but the present claim fixes a linear rate budget with no stochastic row-sum caps and maximizes the continuous-time generator gap. A discrete-time optimizer therefore does not imply the derived budget law, and the general continuous-time SDP formulation itself does not specify its analytic optimal value or all-optima uniqueness.

originality.rationale: Compared the explicit continuous-time priced corona formula and the unrestricted sunlet rigidity statement with the published continuous-time FMMP source, the primary corona spectral theorem, and discrete-time symmetry/SLEM research. Their statements give the optimization framework or spectral ingredients, not the final budget law and rigidity. Search incompleteness remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or privately circulated continuous-time fastest-diffusion results could contain an equivalent corona budget formula.

General SDP and spectral-transfer literature contains key ingredients; novelty is the combined explicit priced optimum and rigidity result, not those ingredients.

value.rationale: The statement provides an exact scalable all-weight budget optimum across every connected vertex-and-edge-transitive core and proves global uniqueness on the nontrivial sunlet family. The exact one-over-size optimal funding law for indispensable leaf edges is a useful network resource-design principle, not a computed table or an unmotivated cutoff.
